name: Bánh Xèo (Vietnamese Sizzling Crepe)
ingredients: 1 head of mustard greens or leaf lettuce
1/2 cup prepared Nước Chấm (sweet and sour fish dipping sauce)
cookingMethod:
1
Prepare the Batter

In a large bowl, whisk together the rice flour and turmeric powder. Gradually pour in the coconut milk and ice-cold water, whisking until smooth and no lumps remain. Stir in the chopped scallions and let the batter rest for at least 30 minutes.
2
Cook the Protein

Heat a wide, non-stick skillet or wok over medium-high heat with a little bit of vegetable oil. Add a few slices of pork belly and a couple of shrimp. Sauté until the pork is browned and the shrimp are cooked through and pink.
3
Pour the Batter
Wait for the sizzle!

Give the rested batter a good stir. Pour a ladleful (about 1/3 cup) of batter into the hot skillet. Immediately swirl and tilt the pan so the batter thinly coats the entire bottom and creeps up the sides. It should make a loud sizzling sound ("xèo").
4
Add the Fillings

Scatter a small handful of cooked mung beans and fresh bean sprouts over half of the crepe. Cover the skillet with a lid and cook for 2-3 minutes to steam the bean sprouts and cook the batter through.
5
Crisp and Fold
Take the lid off for maximum crunch

Remove the lid and lower the heat to medium. Drizzle a tiny bit more oil around the edges of the crepe if needed. Let it cook uncovered for another 2-4 minutes until the bottom and edges become deep golden brown and very crispy. Fold the crepe in half over the filling and slide it onto a plate.
6
Serve the Traditional Way

Serve immediately with the lettuce, fresh herbs, and Nước Chấm. To eat, break off a piece of the crispy crepe, wrap it inside a lettuce leaf along with your favorite herbs, and dip it generously into the fish sauce.
